subject: Acme POC: integration plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Simmons <john.simmons@acmecorp.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC: integration plan & success criteria

Hi John / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Wanted to summarize the call and propose next steps for the POC so we can align on success criteria, owners, and a rough timeline. Below is a short recap and an initial integration plan.

Recap / Success criteria (from our convo):
- Core acceptance: Redwood answers contextual product support queries with >= 80% relevance on a held-out test of 250 queries.
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 800ms for single-turn queries at expected concurrency.
- Cost envelope: per-1k-token cost target to be within the numbers we discussed for the POC budget.
- Security: logs and audit must be visible to Acme security team; data residency in us-east-1 for POC.

POC timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria, sign MSA/POC order form.
- Week 1: dev onboarding, service accounts, SDK quickstart, sample ingest of product docs.
- Week 2: integration + initial evaluator run (250 queries).
- Week 3: tune prompts, run full eval, finalize results and next steps.

Integration plan (high level):
- Auth: use API key scoped to Acme POC project (we'll provision a test key and a dedicated org).
- SDKs: official Redwood SDK (node/python) for streaming & retries; we will attach a quickstart bundle.
- API routes: generation endpoint /v1/generate (supports streaming), embeddings /v1/embeddings, and function/tool calling via /v1/chat with function schema.
- Streaming & tool calls: we'll enable streaming and a callback URL for your ingest pipeline; function calling supported for product lookup.

Owners:
- Redwood: Marissa (product lead) + Dev (integration engineer) + Jonas (SRE for env).
- Acme: John (PM) + Priya (Engineering lead).

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the success criteria above or add anything missing?
2) Please share who on your side will own provisioning and whether you prefer us to create the POC org or you will.
3) We'll send the integration plan doc and SDK quickstart in a separate email.

I'll drop the detailed integration plan and a PDF in a follow-up shortly.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: John Simmons <john.simmons@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecorp.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC: integration plan & success criteria

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. This aligns well with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Success criteria: the 80% relevance threshold is fine; can we also add an intent-recognition metric (correctly identify the top intent in 90% of cases)?
- Latency: the 800ms p95 is reasonable at our expected concurrency (~50 concurrent requests) — important to test under load.
- Security: we need proof of SOC2 coverage and a sample audit log schema for the POC.

On provisioning: we can have Acme infra create the test account and service principal — Priya will take point on that. If it's easier, we can also have Redwood spin up a POC org and hand off credentials; either works.

Could you attach a more detailed integration plan (API examples, streaming callback flow, recommended batching settings)? Also we'll need a sample prompt set and evaluator harness to validate the 250 queries.

Preferred kickoff window: week of Apr 5. Does that work for Redwood?

John
John Simmons
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp

John / Priya —

Great — added intent-recognition to the success criteria. We're attaching the integration plan (PDF) and an SDK quickstart bundle (zip) in this thread. High-level technical details are below and in the attachment.

Attachment highlights (redwood-poc-integration-plan-v1.pdf):
- Full evaluator harness description (how to run locally + hosted), sample prompt set, and scoring scripts.
- API examples: POST /v1/chat for tool/function calling, POST /v1/generate for direct generation with streaming=true, POST /v1/embeddings for indexing.
- Streaming model: chunked SSE with token-level events; callback URL optional for server-side ingestion.
- Suggested batching: for QPS <= 50 use single-request streaming; for higher throughput, enable server batching with max_batch_size=8 and max_latency_ms=20.
- Auth & provisioning: steps for creating a scoped API key and linking to Acme's org id.

Owner assignments and immediate next steps:
- Priya: create test org / service principal or confirm if you want us to create it.
- Dev (redwood): will share SDK quickstart and sample code for embedding+search + streaming.
- Marissa: coordinate kickoff scheduling for week of Apr 5.

Please review the PDF and let us know if you need additional technical detail. If the attachments are blocked by your mail filters, we can share a Drive link.

Best —
Marissa

Hi all —

Following up with some tech-specific notes from our side and a small ask to make the integration smoother. I've included sample requests you can try during the POC.

Key tech notes:
- Auth: we'll provide a scoped API key. For server-to-server calls use standard header Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>. For client-side apps use short-lived tokens if needed.
- Streaming: example (curl):
  curl -N \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-4-stream","input":"<query>","stream":true}' \n    https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate

- Function/tool calling: include functions schema in /v1/chat call; we'll return function_call events with arguments to execute product_lookup(product_id). Example payload in attachment.
- Token limits & costs: default token limit for the stream model is 8k tokens; we recommend truncating longer docs and using embeddings for retrieval.

Sample integration checklist:
- [ ] Create POC org and API key (Acme infra or Redwood to provision)
- [ ] Ingest sample product docs (we recommend chunk_size=1k tokens, overlap=200) via /v1/embeddings + your vector store
- [ ] Hook streaming endpoint or use SSE handler to consume tokens client-side
- [ ] Configure function schema for product lookup and test end-to-end

Attaching our SDK quickstart (node + python examples). If you want, I can join a short technical call next week to walk through the quickstart.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Integration Engineer, Redwood Inference
